solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Stake a new note

blocks.note: the article kept as it stands
standard abbreviation for new
the seventh note of the sol-fa scale, also spelt ti

explanation.surface: A gambler puts down money on a fresh banknote.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Note' is almost always a sol-fa syllable (DO, RE, MI, FA, SO, LA, TE) or N in crosswords, rarely money.
explanation.definitionFit: In poker the ante is the stake each player puts into the pot before the cards are dealt.

clue.text: Value a very quiet increase in salary

blocks.note: the article kept as it stands
pianissimo, the musical marking for very soft playing
a pay rise, in American usage a raise

explanation.surface: Someone quietly slips a worker a small pay increase.
explanation.walkthrough: PP (pianissimo) for 'very quiet' is a standard musical abbreviation, alongside P for quiet.
explanation.definitionFit: To appraise something is to assess its worth, so the verb value is a straight synonym.

clue.text: Skimpy garment a great many have thrown right out

indicators.note: something thrown out is removed, and here the thing ejected is the letter standing for right

blocks.note: a throng is a large crowd
R is the usual abbreviation for right, and it is removed

explanation.surface: Lots of people have tossed out some very skimpy underwear.
explanation.walkthrough: THRONG loses its R to give THONG.
explanation.definitionFit: A thong is minimal underwear or swimwear with a narrow strip at the back, about as skimpy as clothing gets.

clue.text: Act of taking over commercial selection

blocks.note: a television commercial is an ad
an option is a choice or selection

explanation.surface: A business takeover is described as a commercial choice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Commercial' reads as an adjective qualifying 'selection' but is the noun meaning an advertisement.
explanation.definitionFit: Adoption is the taking on or embracing of something, such as a policy or child, as one's own.

clue.text: Clashing recipe with part of octopus and a lot of onion put before us

indicators.note: a lot of something is most but not all of it, so the vegetable word is cut short

blocks.note: a dish is a prepared recipe
an octopus has eight arms
onion without its final letter
the word kept as it stands

explanation.surface: An odd recipe combining octopus and onion is served to us.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put before us' just tells you the onion piece comes ahead of US in the chain.
explanation.definitionFit: Clashing things lack harmony, so they are discordant or out of tune with each other.

clue.text: Fruit black? Exactly!

blocks.note: a plum is a stone fruit
B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether the fruit is black and gets an emphatic yes.
explanation.walkthrough: The exclamation is fair: 'plumb in the middle' uses the word as an adverb meaning precisely.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adverb, plumb means precisely or dead on, as in plumb centre, matching the emphatic exactly.

clue.text: Non-fire? That’s wrong

indicators.note: if the letters are wrong they must be put right by rearranging them

blocks.note: the seven letters of the invented word, hyphen dropped

explanation.surface: Someone scoffs at a claim that a blaze is not a fire.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is also the definition: calling a huge blaze a non-fire is plainly wrong.
explanation.definitionFit: An inferno is a raging blaze, the very opposite of anything that could be called no fire.

clue.text: Fruit mostly smelt awful when brought up

indicators.note: mostly means all but a little, so the last letter of the smell word is lost
in a down clue, bringing something up turns it to read from bottom to top

blocks.note: stunk, meaning smelt awful, without its last letter

explanation.surface: Some fruit gave off a nasty smell when it was served up.
explanation.walkthrough: The second 'Fruit' in this puzzle; here it is the definition, and nuts count botanically as fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: Botanically a nut is a dry fruit with a hard shell, so nuts are a kind of fruit.

clue.text: Change one’s mind regarding church fast

blocks.note: re means concerning or regarding
the forty-day Christian period of fasting before Easter

explanation.surface: Someone reconsiders their view on a church's fasting rules.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fast' reads as quick but is the noun for abstaining from food.
explanation.definitionFit: To relent is to soften and give way after refusing, which means reversing a decision you had made.

clue.text: Deal with company backed in printed media

indicators.note: backed means sent backwards, so the firm's abbreviation is read in reverse
the reversed firm sits inside the word for the newspapers

blocks.note: standard abbreviation for company
the press means newspapers and magazines

explanation.surface: A deal with a firm that has supported the newspapers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Backed' looks like financial support for the company but tells you to reverse CO.
explanation.definitionFit: To process an application or request is to handle it or deal with it formally.

clue.text: Female in army group is out of condition

indicators.note: the woman's single letter sits inside the military group

blocks.note: standard abbreviation for female
a unit is a military formation

explanation.surface: A woman in a military unit has let her fitness slip.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is all army; the woman is only her initial letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Being out of condition means lacking physical fitness, the everyday sense of unfit.

clue.text: Dispute in Camargue when river’s blocked

indicators.note: blocked here means stopped from entering, so the river is shut out of the place name

blocks.note: the Camargue is a marshy region of the Rhône delta in southern France
the Cam is the river through Cambridge, and it is taken away

explanation.surface: A row breaks out in the Camargue when a river is dammed.
explanation.walkthrough: The Cam, Cambridge's river, is a crossword favourite; removing it from CAMARGUE leaves the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To dispute a point is to argue about it or contest it, so the verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: Reddish-brown and gold stream

blocks.note: Au is the chemical symbol for gold
burn is a Scottish and northern English word for a stream

explanation.surface: A stream runs rust-coloured and golden, perhaps with iron and sunlight.
explanation.walkthrough: A burn is a small stream in Scotland and northern England; nothing to do with fire.
explanation.definitionFit: Auburn describes hair of a reddish-brown shade, so the colour description is an exact match.

clue.text: Pressure initially seems to change unknown instrument

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of the word right beside it

blocks.note: standard abbreviation for pressure in physics
the opening letter of seems
to alter is to change
x, y and z are the algebraic unknowns

explanation.surface: Pressure at first seems to change an unknown musical instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: The mathematical unknowns X, Y and Z are standard crossword letters; here it is Y.
explanation.definitionFit: A psaltery is an ancient stringed musical instrument plucked with the fingers, like a small zither.

clue.text: Affecting moral superiority to nuncio’s aims for reform

indicators.note: reform means form again, so the letters are reshaped into a new word

blocks.note: thirteen letters of fodder, apostrophe dropped

explanation.surface: A self-righteous attitude towards a papal envoy's reforming goals.
explanation.walkthrough: A nuncio is a papal ambassador, which suits the churchy surface; 'to' belongs to the fodder, not a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Sanctimonious people put on a show of being holier and more virtuous than everyone else.

clue.text: Lack of wisdom I test in statement of denial

indicators.note: the pronoun and the checking verb go inside the word for no

blocks.note: the pronoun kept as it stands
to vet is to check or examine
nay is an old word for no

explanation.surface: Someone foolishly takes a test while insisting on their denial.
explanation.walkthrough: NAY is an old-fashioned no, still heard in parliamentary votes (the ayes and the nays); VET, for test, is a vet's examination of an animal.
explanation.definitionFit: Naivety is innocent inexperience, a want of worldly judgement, so it amounts to a shortage of wisdom.

clue.text: One regularly uncovered chap in barrel turning up

indicators.note: the man's name goes inside the big cask
in a down clue, turning up flips the letters to read from the bottom

blocks.note: a tun is a large cask for wine or beer
a typical crossword man's name

explanation.surface: A man hidden in a barrel keeps popping up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Regularly' tempts you to take alternate letters, but here it just means habitually and belongs to the definition. SID is the stock crossword chap.
explanation.definitionFit: A nudist habitually goes without clothes, so is often left bare as a matter of routine.

clue.text: Young cat – chap embraces it tons

indicators.note: to embrace is to hold within, so the man's name wraps round what follows

blocks.note: a typical crossword man's name
the pronoun kept as it stands
T is the abbreviation for tons

explanation.surface: A man cuddles a young cat an enormous amount.
explanation.walkthrough: KEN, like SID and ED, is one of the stock short names crosswords use for 'chap'.
explanation.definitionFit: A kitten is the offspring of a cat, the standard word for one that is not yet grown.

clue.text: Time to crush online troublemaker

blocks.note: standard abbreviation for time
to roll something flat is to crush it

explanation.surface: It is time to stamp out an internet pest.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface asks you to crush the troublemaker; really the verb is ROLL, as with a roller.
explanation.definitionFit: An internet troll posts provocative messages deliberately to upset people and disrupt discussions.

clue.text: Weld remade around ring for fixing pin

indicators.note: something remade is put together again in a different form
the shuffled joining word goes round the circular letter

blocks.note: the word itself, as fodder
a ring is round, like the letter O

explanation.surface: A metalworker redoes a weld around a ring to secure a pin.
explanation.walkthrough: WELD rearranged as DWEL, then split round the O.
explanation.definitionFit: A dowel is a headless wooden or metal peg used to join two pieces, a fastening pin.

clue.text: Large mammal is healthy when putting on weight

indicators.note: putting something on is wearing it around you, so the healthy word is wrapped in the weight letter

blocks.note: standard abbreviation for weight
hale means fit and healthy, as in hale and hearty

explanation.surface: A big animal stays well even as it gains weight.
explanation.walkthrough: W wraps round HALE; since W sits at the edge, it reads like a simple join.
explanation.definitionFit: Whales are the largest of all mammals, the blue whale being the biggest animal ever known.

clue.text: Steep cliff is mostly frightening

indicators.note: mostly means all but a bit, so the final letter of the fear word goes

blocks.note: scary without its final letter

explanation.surface: A sheer cliff face is rather terrifying.
explanation.walkthrough: SCARY loses its Y.
explanation.definitionFit: A scar, also spelt scaur, is a steep rocky outcrop or crag on a hillside, especially in northern England.

clue.text: Caught looking embarrassed over initially expression of belief

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of the word just before it

blocks.note: C is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught
an embarrassed face goes red
the opening letter of over

explanation.surface: Someone caught out blushes at their own profession of faith.
explanation.walkthrough: C for caught comes from cricket scoring, where a batsman's dismissal is recorded that way.
explanation.definitionFit: A credo is a creed, a set of principles, from the Latin for I believe.

clue.text: Individual’s trapped male deer – a tragedy may unfold here

indicators.note: the apostrophe s stands for has, so the single thing has trapped the animal inside it

blocks.note: an individual is one
a stag is a male deer

explanation.surface: A stag is caught in a trap, and a sad ending looms.
explanation.walkthrough: The ’s is 'has', not a possessive: ONE has trapped STAG. The tragedy is a play, not the deer's fate.
explanation.definitionFit: A theatrical tragedy is performed on stage, the place where such a drama plays out before an audience.

clue.text: Solitary revolutionary supporter of Charles 1

indicators.note: a revolutionary word turns its letters around into a new order

blocks.note: eight letters of fodder

explanation.surface: A lone rebel who backs King Charles I.
explanation.walkthrough: The joke is that a revolutionary is the last thing a king's supporter would be. Charles I lost the English Civil War to Parliament.
explanation.definitionFit: In the English Civil War the royalists, or Cavaliers, fought for the king against Parliament.

clue.text: Refuse dumped beside northern motorway, last of all

indicators.note: last of all means the closing letter of every one of the words before it

blocks.note: the final letters of the four words

explanation.surface: Rubbish is fly-tipped next to a motorway in the north.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Refuse' reads as rubbish, but it is the verb to decline.
explanation.definitionFit: To refuse a request is to deny it, withholding what was asked for.
